index_record.dataset_generation_caption: The figure illustrates the process of assigning an orientation to the edges of a minimum spanning tree T_m^1, transforming it into a directed graph. The global layout consists of two side-by-side diagrams connected by a rightward arrow, indicating a transformation from an undirected to a directed structure. The left diagram shows an undirected graph composed of black lines connecting black circular nodes labeled v_1^1 through v_9^1, forming a diamond-like lattice structure. Three specific nodes—v_1^1, v_5^1, and v_9^1—are highlighted with purple circles and labeled p_11^1, p_12^1, and p_13^1 respectively, suggesting they are points of interest or designated vertices. The right diagram represents the same underlying graph but with directed edges indicated by arrows on the purple lines connecting the purple-labeled nodes. These directed edges are labeled e_1 through e_5, each pointing from one purple node to another, establishing a flow direction. The orientation is determined by designating p_11^1 as the source vertex and all other vertices as sinks, meaning all edges emanate from p_11^1 or are oriented toward sinks. The visual modules include black circular nodes for general vertices, purple circular nodes for special vertices (p_11^1, p_12^1, p_13^1), black lines for undirected edges, and purple lines with arrows for directed edges. Text labels are placed near nodes and edges in purple font for emphasis. The connections between nodes are shown via straight black or purple lines; in the right diagram, arrows on the purple lines indicate the directionality imposed by the orientation rule. The transformation arrow between the two diagrams signifies the application of the orientation algorithm, which assigns directions to edges based on the source-sink configuration.
